chunks: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.
Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born. Nor is there to Him any equivalent.

key_terms.اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ: Allah, the Eternal Refuge / The Self-Sufficient

ai.seo_question: What is the theological significance of Surah Al-Ikhlas in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Kamal al-Din, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this recitation as a foundational proof of Tawhid, emphasizing Allah's absolute self-sufficiency (Al-Samad) and lack of progeny to counter Christian and polytheist claims. This chapter serves as a concise theological summary of divine attributes, often recited in daily prayers to affirm monotheism against shirk. The emphasis on 'no equal' (Kufu) reinforces the exclusivity of divine worship in Shia creed.
